the Calvin-cycle enzymes RuBisCO (ribulose-1-5-bisphosphatase carboxylase) and PRK (phosphoribulokinases) are able to replace the glycerol-forming pathway for maintaining redox balance in S. cereviase, and that this replacement is possible without affecting growth rate, if the enzymes are expressed at high levels and the cells are grown at high dilution rates.

a combination of metabolic engineering strategies, including the expression of Calvin cycle enzymes, the deletion of GPD1 and GPD2, the overexpression of the non- oxidative pentose phosphate pathway, and the overexpression of GroEL and GroES, can enable the production of ethanol from glucose in S. cereviase without the production of glycerol.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to improve the ethanol yield, it is necessary to reduce the glycerol production rate to levels comparable to those of the wild type, which requires the use of a strain with an optimal rate of growth.
